source.title: Black-Box Generalization
source.authors: Konstantinos E. Nikolakakis; Farzin Haddadpour; Dionysios S. Kalogerias; Amin Karbasi

record.file_problem: Full text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives generalization bounds for zeroth-order learning and reports that its mini-batch bounds are independent of batch size, extending batch-size analysis to ZoSS under theoretical assumptions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds, not empirical held-out errors. It does not test memorization, neural-network architectures, optimizer rankings, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study derives stability-based upper bounds for ZoSS and SGD, not batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets. Identical upper bounds across batch sizes do not establish identical actual generalization gaps or test errors. No own result tests V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate when restricted to bounds: under Lipschitz and smooth losses and appropriate learning-rate and smoothing choices, ZoSS achieves generalization upper bounds matching SGD's; the mini-batch unbounded-loss bounds are independent of batch size. These results do not prove equality of actual held-out performance across batch sizes.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes zeroth-order ZoSS rather than standard gradient methods and reports stability-based theoretical bounds rather than empirical train and test errors.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that the mini-batch generalization bound is independent of batch size; bounds also depend on loss assumptions and learning-rate choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 10 extends the unbounded-loss generalization upper bounds of Theorems 7 and 8 to every mini-batch size m ≤ n. Limits recover corresponding mini-batch SGD and full-batch GD guarantees.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under Lipschitz and smooth loss assumptions and specified learning-rate and smoothing choices, ZoSS admits a common stability-based generalization upper bound across batch sizes at a given iteration budget.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical; no empirical held-out performance, training error, or fixed-epoch comparison is reported. Results depend on Lipschitz and smooth loss assumptions and specified learning-rate choices.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible result rows identified. Other theorems report bounds for ZoSS without varying a condition named by the mapped version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier performance and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance and tuning-dependent differences.
Large-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets, including penalties and their recovery through recipe changes or longer training.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking observed generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V5 limits_scope verdict. The introduction's empirical batch-size discussion cites Hoffer et al.; it is not this study's own empirical result.

versions.untested_parts: Network width and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance.
Empirical image-classifier and language-model performance under fixed epoch budgets; the paper studies theoretical ZoSS bounds, not those settings.
Sharpness and other measured properties tracking train-test gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: mini-batch ZoSS
rows.operation_detail: Derives generalization error bounds for mini-batch ZoSS across batch sizes.
rows.measure: Theorem 10 states that the generalization error bounds of Theorems 7 and 8 hold for any batch size.
rows.value: same generalization error bounds for any batch size m ≤ n
rows.note: This is a theoretical bound comparison for ZoSS, not measured performance under a fixed epoch budget.
rows.check: Theorem 10 establishes batch-size-independent upper bounds under Lipschitz and smooth loss assumptions and specified learning rates. It does not establish absence of a large-batch performance penalty. The bounds compare a given iteration budget T, not a fixed epoch budget; held-out performance also depends on optimization error (Section 2, Eq. 2). Retain only as a theoretical finding outside these versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
